question.leadin: He met with Jose de San Martin at the Guayaquil Conference.
question.text: Name this early 19th-century South American leader nicknamed "The Liberator."
question.clue: This man met with a leader who soon retired to Europe at the Guayaquil Conference, and he responded to a message from Henry Cullen with his "Letter From Jamaica"; this man also penned a document explaining a loss, the Cartagena Manifesto.

swap.leadin: As much as 70% of the male population of this country may have been killed in the disastrous War of the Triple Alliance.
swap.text: Name this country which was led by Francisco Solano Lopez from 1862 until he was killed in action in 1870.
swap.clue: Another leader of this country orchestrated the genocide of the Ache people, and a fourth leader of this country sent children with painted-on beards and sticks into battle and had his mother flogged after losing the Siege of Humaita.

question.leadin: The Ipiranga Brook, site of Dom Pedro the First's declaration of independence, flows through a suburb of this city.
question.text: Name this most populous city in the Southern hemisphere, located a few hundred miles west of Rio de Janeiro.
question.clue: In 1922, this state experienced a cultural boom when the Week of Modern Art was held in its capital.

swap.text: Diaz was overthrown by this man who led the Mexican Revolution; he himself was overthrown in 1913 by Huerta and assassinated soon after.
swap.clue: Earlier, he was arrested while running for president for the Nationalist Democratic Party and the National Anti-Reelection Party.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the American colour-coded War Plans.
question.text: The volatile political situation in this country forced America to consider an invasion, codenamed War Plan Green. After this country's revolution ended, the political situation stabilised enough that War Plan Green never had to be put into effect.
question.clue: The German ship SS Ypiranga was seized during the U.S. occupation of a port in this country following the Tampico Affair.
question.set: 2023 Politics & History with a side of Memes

swap.leadin: This leader introduced chewing gum to the United States while in exile there.
swap.text: Name this leader who served as many as eleven terms as president of Mexico in the first half of the 19th century, a number that is debated due to his frequent use of puppet rulers between terms.
swap.answerHtml: Antonio Lopez de Santa Anna [or Antonio de Padua María Severino López de Santa Anna y Pérez de Lebrón]
swap.clue: After receiving a wound in the Pastry War, this leader buried his amputated leg with full military honors.

question.leadin: At the Battle of El Roble, this man gave the order, "Live with honor, or die with glory!"
question.text: Name this founding father of Chile. With the leader of the Army of the Andes, this man helped win the Battle of Chacabuco.
question.clue: He found himself to be increasingly in military and political competition with Jose Miguel Carrera, but was not as prominent as Carrera.

swap.leadin: Governor General Paul Scoon was rescued during an event in this country which saw a successful invasion of an airstrip at Point Salines.
swap.text: Name this country whose leader Hudson Austin was part of its "New Jewel" movement. An invasion of this country was prompted by the execution of Maurice Bishop and was codenamed Operation Urgent Fury.
swap.clue: This island was captured from Lord Macartney by the French during the Revolutionary War and was the site of a naval battle between the grandfather of Lord Byron and the Comte d'Estaing.

question.leadin: This man was promoted to be a member of the Sagunto Dragoons following the Battle of Albuera in Spain.
question.text: Identify this general, who replaced Manuel Belgrano following the Battle of Tucuman. He'd win the Battle of Maipu and liberate Santiago, Chile.
question.clue: This leader defeated Manuel Osorio alongside Bernardo O'Higgins at Maipu after winning at Chacabuco.

swap.leadin: This man's father was arrested for protesting the signing of the Bryan-Chamorro treaty.
swap.text: Name this Nicaraguan guerrilla leader, nicknamed El Chipotle, who was kidnapped and murdered by members of his country's National Guard in 1934 after meeting with President Juan Bautista Sacasa.
swap.answerHtml: Augusto Cesar Sandino [or Augusto Calderon Sandino or Augusto Nicolas Sandino]
swap.clue: At the end of his country's Constitutionalist War, this general refused to lay down his arms and instead waged a guerrilla war against the U.S. Marines occupying his country.

question.leadin: This man led the "Revolt of the Sergeants" that toppled Gerardo Machado's government.
question.text: Name this world leader who cultivated alliances with gangsters like Meyer Lansky. The 26th of July Movement opposed this man, and a revolution against him began with the 1953 raid on the Moncada Barracks.
question.clue: The Hotel Nacional in this leader's capital played host to a meeting of mafia members Meyer Lansky and Lucky Luciano.

swap.text: Jose Napoleon Duarte presided throughout much of a twelve-year civil war in this Central American country. In this country, the politically active Archbishop Oscar Romero was killed at the altar.
swap.answerHtml: Republic of El Salvador [or Republica de El Salvador]
swap.clue: The killing of Rutilio Grande in this country prompted liberation theologian, Archbishop Oscar Romero, to refuse to attend state occasions.

question.leadin: Philip II referred to the conflict against these people as the "Indian Flanders" due to the number of Spanish soldiers they killed.
question.text: Name these native people of Chile and Argentina, who forced the destruction of the Seven Cities during the Arauco War under the leadership of Toqui like Caupolican.
question.clue: Unrest among these people caused the "destruction of the seven cities" south of the Biobio River.

swap.text: This man led troops in support of Juan Bautista Sacasa. Upon the intervention of US Marines, he fled to the mountains to lead a guerilla campaign. He gave his name to a later armed movement opposed by the Contras.
swap.clue: This man took up arms to support the presidential claim of Juan Bautista Sacasa and successfully evaded US Marine efforts to capture him.

question.leadin: This conflict was fought over access to minerals in the Atacama Desert.
question.text: Name this conflict, fought between 1879 and 1883, in which Bolivia and Peru were defeated by Chile.

swap.leadin: The term for this system derives from the Spanish verb meaning "to entrust."
swap.text: Name this New World labor system that entrusted natives to Spaniards to protect and convert, though in practice it was simply slave labor. It was based on the adelantado system of the Reconquista.
swap.clue: This system was gradually phased out after the passage of the New Laws under Charles I, which replaced this system with the repartimiento system.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Caribbean Legion, a group of Latin American leaders and exiles in the 40s and 50s, including a young Fidel Castro, that aimed to eliminate dictatorships in the region.
question.text: One of the Legion's biggest successes was this leader's overthrow of Teodoro Picado in the Costa Rican Civil War. He then abolished Costa Rica's armed forces and granted women and Afro-Costa Ricans the right to vote.
question.answerHtml: José Figueres Ferrer [accept either underlined portion; accept “Don Pepe;” reject “José María Figueres,” as that’s his son who was president from 1994–98]
question.clue: In the first of his three terms, this President of Costa Rica disbanded the military, and had earlier deployed the Caribbean Legion to overthrow Teodoro Picado during the 1948 civil war. This president also granted women and Afro-Costa Ricans the right to vote.

swap.text: In 1894, this Liberal president of Nicaragua seized the British protectorate claimed by Zambos or African pirates at Greytown. He then made overtures to France on deals to build a canal, prompting the U.S. to fund his political opponents.
swap.clue: This man annexed the Mosquito Coast and installed Miguel Davila as president of Honduras while serving as president of Nicaragua from 1893 to 1910, when the arrival of US Marines forced him to flee.

question.text: The brouhaha erupted when a Paraguayan gunboat opened fire on this U.S. ship captained by Thomas Page, which was on a scientific expedition in the area, resulting in the death of an American seaman.

swap.text: Morinigo led his expedition to Cerro Cora during a 1936 revolution in Paraguay named for this month, in which Rafael Franco overthrew Eusebio Ayala. Franco went on to found a Revolutionary Party named after this month in 1951.
swap.answerHtml: February [or the February Revolution or the Revolutionary Febrerista Party]
swap.clue: That revolution named for this month was followed by the June Days and created the Second French Republic, thus ending the Orleans monarchy by forcing Louis Philippe's abdication.
